# Multi-Level Implementation Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the phase sequence in the RFC into **independently committable and independently
> verifiable** three-level tasks.
>
> The phase order and acceptance gates are governed solely by the main body of RFC-039. This
> document is responsible only for decomposing the work into an executable granularity and
> registering conflicts that remain unadjudicated.

**Numbering gaps (not reclaimed)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`. None of the three
has had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the history of this document has zero
hits for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used to verify this),
and there are no references elsewhere in the repository. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of
`05` (test revival and completion): that phase has already been split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and
`8.8`, so P8's numbering is aligned with its phase number (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so
on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for the tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
rationale for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered Level 2/Level 3 row
**must contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P phase to which it truly belongs, which may
differ from its section) and “**Blocks the mainline**.” `Registered, awaiting scheduling` is no
longer the default state; an unmarked task is treated as **not schedulable**. Numbers must be
**unique across the entire document** (tasks on different tracks use their track number, such as
`029g.x`, and must not occupy an `N.x` number). **Check-off/completion registration is based on
“task ID + evidence (gate metrics, run ID, issue number, file:line)”**, not commit
IDs—`pull --rebase` rewrites local hashes, so hard-coded IDs inevitably become invalid (2026-10-13
example: `94ad03ce4`→`631eb3e3c`). Use `git log` to find commit IDs.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Highlights” of eight documents into this master table,
**five hard gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been closed:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Resolution                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever.** RFC-039 defines P5 (splitting the checker) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how to perform the split; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one `annotations.rs` line, which is the only mention in the entire batch                                                     | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                                                            |
| G2  | **The `include!` migration has three claimed owners and zero implementations.** RFC-039 places it in P4; `02` assigns it to itself; `06` S7 also lists it. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) does **not** include `semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                                                                 | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 in this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here                                       |
| G3  | **Three coexisting inventories of CI scripts.** RFC-039 lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists 4 checks under entirely different names; `04` additionally requires `check-synth-boundary.py`. After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified inventory**; `check-obligations.py` has dual ownership in P4 and P9 | See §P9 of this document for the unified inventory (11 scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents now refer to this table                                             |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`.** `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum”; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                | **Revive in P1, delete with Pratt in P8** (decision registered as C1)—first restore CI coverage, then perform the deletion in 8.6 in P8 together with the Pratt dead-code removal |
| G5  | **Conflicting descriptions of the L2 target.** RFC-039 and this directory's index say “grammar-driven syntax,” but `05` self-assesses: “**We have not adopted true grammar-driven parsing (LALRPOP); we have only implemented declarative table lookup**”                                                                                                                              | Converged on **full LALRPOP grammar-driven parsing** (`05` §Syntax: full grammar-driven parsing); the G7/G8 acceptance gates enforce that commitment                              |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0  仓库维护机制与代码放置规程     08        ← 新增，先立规矩
P1  复活孤儿测试并修缺陷           06 §S1
P2  建立等价性判据基线             07 全部
P3  修正确性漏洞（最小方案）        02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4  阶段契约与统一 Driver          02
P5  checker 文件内拆分             02 + 本文补齐
P6  类型表示单一化                 03
P7  中间表示 SSA 化                04      } 可并行
P8  前端范式变更                   05      }
P9  防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单）     01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正             06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions—no fabrication, no endless filling, and no
patching when a refactor is required—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before work begins; otherwise, while reviving tests in P1, work would already be adding `mod`
declarations to `tests/mod.rs`, which is precisely the source of the G4 conflict.

> **There is no size-baseline task.** On 2026-10-03, a decision canceled every line-count / size
> gate. Size problems are to be solved through separation of responsibilities (see `08` Prohibition
> 2, criterion A, which requires human judgment). **0.2.1 is the core acceptance criterion for this
> phase**: if the gate cannot report the known parallel representations, the criterion design is
> wrong and the gate is a false gate.

> phase discovers a defect for which “the old behavior did not count as success”—**A silent failure
> / B silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss of control** (crash, stack
> exhaustion, silently incorrect result)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactor**, but all four
> requirements are mandatory: ① red first, then green (the red criterion must exist first and must
> actually be red); ② the externally visible behavior of programs that “previously compiled
> successfully and ran correctly” must not change (they must not start failing, and their existing
> diagnostic codes/messages/exit codes must not be changed or removed); ③ register it in the same
> commit (this row must identify the defect class + include a revision note for that phase + the
> PR's required block must include the “Defect class” line); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same
> commit + manually review the diff. **The three categories D user-visible semantics / E external
> contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must still receive a user decision first.** See

> the A–F allowlist; **the “default super-refactor + post-hoc registration” approach is not
> adopted** (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes cannot be distinguished
> from regressions, and this conflicts with “there is no C5′” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted on 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by the
ordering constraint**; it is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (narrowing
Rust's `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed as a whole before P4**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps the rewrite
surface of 4 refactoring phases; reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and baseline
updates on the new grammar / checker layout / SSA IR.

never consumed anywhere in the repository) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4's 4.3
obligation ledger loses one “produced but never consumed” field.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red first, then green**: each of the 2 behavioral changes must have its red criterion committed
   before the code is changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ②
   unreferenced top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously pub items were
   absolutely exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixtures, they must be replaced by
   equivalent new cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: overlaps with 3.4 files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be sequential
and cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; the implementer chooses which to perform first based on the context at hand.

> **Commit correspondence (2026-10-08)**: when the worktree was swept during parallel work, this
> section's incorporation (the P3.5 chapter + the main-chain/constraint row) was merged into
> `97071c81b` together with RFC-039's D56, although that commit's message records only “3.4 addendum
> registration + D57/D58 decision filing” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten;
> following the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 implementation note), it
> is registered in place as a post-hoc bisection marker.

|                             | 5.2.2 Consolidate the refinement entry point as “`&self` + return diagnostics,” **without leaving impl**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer writes to the error channel implicitly through `&mut self`; the diagnostic set is returned upward, and the sole write point is the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Rationale for not leaving impl**: this family's field surface consists only of `self.env` (so leaving impl is technically feasible), but converting “the entry point and the whole walk” to free functions would move the call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 production sites (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 production sites + 1 test, and would create a “shared surface (signature collection) → refinement” reverse dependency—the opposite of the coupling this step is intended to eliminate | 5.2.1        | C1 zero-diff; 4 **symbolic criteria**: ① the signature contains no `&mut self` ② the function body contains no `env.errors` ③ the diagnostic write point for the **returned entry point** exists only in the caller ④ the entry point still has exactly 1 location |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move out the 10-member annotation-validation family (now the single file `checker/annotations.rs`; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 members are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a free function within the family)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | 5.2.2        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                             | 5.3.2 **Keep `collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) as `pub(crate)` and under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 **did not move it** based on measurement ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a new `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is moved with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` so that this import remains byte-for-byte unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | 5.3.1        | **Zero caller changes** is this step's hard acceptance criterion: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty                                                                                                                          |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, `checker.rs` **must** add
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` so that this import remains byte-for-byte unchanged; measurement
showed that 5.3 did **not** move it, so this batch did not add a re-export (the criterion was
already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines—this adds
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and provides zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split when the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**Hard acceptance** (**criterion revised on 2026-10-27, following decision ② on 2026-10-26**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be empty in **every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files under `tests/`** (tests that directly exercise changed code,
such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be changed when mechanically required, but each change
must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted and assertions
must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new diagnostic code +
baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is a separate round with a
separate decision.

> **Revision relationship**: the original criterion (decision ② on 2026-10-26) was written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-difference requirement to the entire
> `tests/` directory. The revised criterion changes only direct-drive test files from “zero
> difference” to “may be changed, but file / line count / reason must be registered.” The **corpus
> layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library (`src/std/`)
> retain their zero-difference requirements**. First application = 6.1.2: only
> `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed by **3 lines** (2 `assert_format_eq` occurrences changed
> from `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment), with the rationale = the changed spelling requires the expected
> type name in the assertion to be updated in sync; no tests were deleted and no assertions were
> weakened. See 09a “P6 6.1 Name Canonicalization Closure”.

**Risk**: 8.4's dual-parser differential is an **unskippable equivalence gate**. If it finds
non-equivalence, the problem must be solved before the 8.5 traffic switch, rather than hidden after
the switch with C5′. Missing one of the approximately 89 BP reference migrations in 8.6 will
**silently change associativity** (no error, only a changed parse result).

> **8.3–8.6 depend on `08`'s D0/D2**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or the action
> code refers backward to `sema`, `check-boundary.py` will block it.

### P9 Anti-Rebound Gates (Unified Script Inventory — This Document Supplies the Original Gap G3)

Source: [01](01-routing.md) §Anti-Rebound Mechanism + [08](08-maintenance-mechanism.md)
§Machine-Checkable Rules

**This is the sole authoritative inventory of all CI scripts** (11 scripts). Scripts are connected
to CI at their “introduction phase”; those marked report-only are uniformly converted to hard
failures in P9 (changing “report” to “fail”)—existing violations (parallel representations,
disambiguation aliases, etc.) cannot reach zero until P6/P8, and converting them early would keep CI
permanently red and lead to humans bypassing the gates. When P9 converts them to hard failures, the
gates should be exactly green. P2's 2.5, P4's 4.3.2, and P7's 7c.1 refer to this table and do not
maintain separate inventories.

- [ ] **9.1–9.11 Connect the 11 scripts at their introduction phases and convert them uniformly to
      hard failures in P9** (details in the table below)
- [x] **9.12 Prerequisite for hard conversion: rebaseline criterion C wiring points and clear the
      stale inventory** (2 Level 3 tasks, **registered and closed on 2026-10-26**): the title used
      at registration, “clear existing duplicate same-name definitions,” was a
      **mislabel**—`--strict` violations came only from criterion C (entry wiring), while criterion
      A (same-name definitions, 181 entries) is report-only and never turns `--strict` red; this was
      corrected during closure. Root cause: `STAGE_MARKERS` was calibrated on 2026-10-06 against the
      pre-P4 state where “6 paths were each wired manually”; its comment explicitly states “after P4
      unified the Driver, this table will be deleted together with the inventory,” but after P4
      landed, neither the vocabulary nor the 19 `KNOWN_WIRING_SITES` were retired. Consequently, the
      criterion judged the Driver's **own stage table** (`Stage::DeadCodeAnalysis` variant name,
      `slug` string table, `state.rs` dependency table) to be violations—the exact opposite of
      Prohibition 3 criterion C (“adding the Nth entry **instead of registering it in the
      declarative stage table** → violation”). Disposition = **rebaseline the criterion** rather
      than add allowlists. Result: `--strict` violations 9→0, inventory 19→**7**, measured wiring
      points 18→**8** (7 inventory + 1 dispatch point), criterion-A same-name definitions 181→180
      (deleting the `build_registry` entry), and `pub(crate)` 167→166. **Owning phase: P9; Blocks
      the mainline: No (blocks hard conversion in P9).**
  - 9.12.1 Rebaseline delivery (4 commits, itemized in the closure record in
    [09a](./09a-wbs-history.md)): ① **rebaseline the criterion**—merge LEX into `Parsing`
    (`src/driver/stage.rs` and 02 §Target Design 1 both state that `Parsing` = “lexical + syntactic
    analysis (lex → parse)”), make DEADCODE/MONO recognize only call forms, exempt
    `#[cfg(test)] mod` by determining scope through **brace pairing**, separate `dispatch` as
    `DECLARED_DISPATCH_POINTS`, and clear 13 stale inventory entries (each with a removal reason,
    divided by measurement into 3 categories: 5 functions deleted / 5 functions still present but no
    longer with a stage primitive / 3 demoted to a single stage solely because LEX was merged); ②
    **derive arm shapes**—the 12 `self.<arm>(` forms are derived from the exhaustive match in
    `dispatch` (`Stage::ALL` provides the variants, a single source) + 3 fail-loud guards (variant
    source invalid / arm not found / arm has no `fn` definition), and fix the false positive caused
    by counting the signature line in the tested body, which caused `fn check_project(` to match TC
    itself (the `fn_body` strips the signature section; measured “≥2 → <2 stages” reduction = 0); ③
    **state coverage as fact**—the stage implementations of 4 variants (VendorConsistency /
    Discovery / Registry / RoleClassification) are shared primitives outside the Driver and are
    registered as known blind spots; ④ **describe blind spots by nature**—live wiring
    (`collect_package_refs`, called from `driver/arms.rs:626`) and dead-code candidates
    (`build_registry`, zero callers) must not receive the same treatment. Three independent reviews
    all returned needs_revision (medium → medium → low; all 3 findings were genuinely fixed), and
    the 4th round **passed** with no findings. **Acceptance**:
    `python scripts/ci/check-fanout.py --strict` exit 0 (0 violations / 6 inventory entries / 1
    dispatch point) ✅
  - 9.12.2 Expand criterion C coverage and clear `build_registry` (**completed; closed on
    2026-10-26**; user decisions **D1-A retain + D2-A delete**): ① **delete** the zero-caller chain

    was a **lib-target public item**, and deletion was separately adjudicated as an external
    API-surface change. ② **retain** the Driver-external stage primitives that still exist after
    deletion: VendorConsistency ← `ensure_vendor_consistency`, Discovery ← `discover_with_used`,
    RoleClassification ← `roles::classify` (narrowed to the qualified form—a bare name would
    incorrectly catch same-named helpers elsewhere; the constructed counterexample reproduces), and
    Registry ← `extract_module_info` (does not use bare `.register(`, which occurs in many

    167→166 (the necessary result of deleting `discover`). Review chain: round 1 needs_revision (1

## Implementation Highlights: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Sequential Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 hemorrhage-stopping channel (decision on 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus tier + 2 red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) can proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping correctness vulnerabilities is not blocked by criterion-infrastructure
> construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver requires all 3
> layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The 3 prohibitions constrain every P1 action (1.2.x is exactly the act of adding `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                           |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baselines                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must be **written as red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus tier (2.3.2) must exist so the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                               |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order lets the stage table fossilize bugs as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                             |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g's (#399) deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (see the inventory in this document's §P3.5)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56) |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` migration and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                           |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations are not converged first, the new IR will grow into a third representation                                                                                                                                                          |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                      |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                      | Members                                                                        | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC-039)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                        | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                           |
| B                                          | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                  | Each independently adds `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| C                                          | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                | The 3 layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D                                          | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                 | `02` explicitly states that S5 “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| E                                          | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                          | All are mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| F                                          | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the 3 scripts introduced in P0 can be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| G                                          | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                   | Disjoint file sets (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies 2 `pub` locations in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pair overlaps) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same batch); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (unified into P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` / `environment.rs` are
the same files—the external track's pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel fixes must be
sequential).

**New internal document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly sequential;
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly sequential, and 7b's `Phi` arm must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is a separate phase rather than being merged into P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while
  rules are “pre-hoc judgment.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was required”;
  only the D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative inventory of CI scripts**—the 3 coexisting inventories under
  original gap G3 made closure impossible. This table merges them, with 11 scripts each owned by one
  phase and explicit report-only states and hard-conversion points.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to do after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactor means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status corrections into S4.
- **P5's steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the rollback granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertable.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the fixed defects
  must not be reverted” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution convention**:
  every 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect description as a
  post-hoc bisection marker.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as 2 exclusive commits
  under DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse**—about 89 renamed references; missing one **silently changes
  associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, with the deletion
  action left to P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally planned as an “independent issue”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core
  language semantics and must not be left as an unimplemented residual.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into the
  generation-time gate task in P10 S6.
